nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a finite set of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$. Then $S$ contains a multicolored sunflower if there are triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with $x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.
nodes.title: Multicolored sunflower

nodes.summary: There are a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n > n_0$, every finite set $S$ of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ with $x + y + z = 0$ for every $(x, y, z) \in S$ and with $|S| \ge 3^{(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ contains a multicolored sunflower: triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with $x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.
nodes.title: The multicolored sunflower conjecture holds
